extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors, inventor groups, inventor-owned small businesses seeking PTAB pro bono assistance; and registered patent practitioners interested in volunteering
extracted.subtask_short: PTAB pro bono eligibility and application
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility criteria and application/volunteer guidance for the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) Pro Bono Program for independent inventors, inventor groups, and inventor-owned small businesses seeking free legal assistance for ex parte appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scope / supported applicant types
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB Pro Bono Program supports solo inventors, inventor groups, and inventor-owned small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches volunteer patent professionals with financially under-resourced inventors, inventor groups, and inventor-owned small businesses to provide free legal assistance in preparing ex parte appeals to the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be exactly one known inventor for the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must reside in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Income threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must have a total household income of less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines (Modified as of April 1, 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Knowledge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must demonstrate knowledge of the ex parte appeal process by successfully completing a video training course consisting of two videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first video explains how the PTAB Pro Bono Program works. The second video walks through the ex parte appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must apply to the program within one month from the date of an office action in which the claims have been twice or finally rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — Ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the application or resulting patent to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity status note
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-Entity Status — Eliminated as of April 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously relevant micro-entity considerations are no longer applicable as of the stated date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no more than four known inventors for the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Residency (individual requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must reside in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Income threshold (individual requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must have a total household income of less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Knowledge requirement (individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must demonstrate knowledge of the ex parte appeal process by successfully completing the two-video training course (program overview and ex parte appeal walkthrough).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventors must apply to the program within one month from the date of an office action in which the claims have been twice or finally rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor group — Ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor or the inventor group must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the application or resulting patent to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Inventor ownership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The small business must be 100% inventor owned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no more than four known inventors of the inventor-owned business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Assignment to organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must agree to assign his/her rights to the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Residency and principal place of business
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must reside in the United States and the principal place of business of the inventor-owned small business must be in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Income threshold (individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must have a total household income of less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Knowledge requirement (individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must demonstrate knowledge of the ex parte appeal process by successfully completing the two-video training course (program overview and ex parte appeal walkthrough).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor-owned small business must apply to the program within 1 month from the date of an office action in which the claims have been twice or finally rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Previous year business income
rubrics_metrics.description: If the business was operating in the preceding calendar year, the business must have had a total gross income of less than $150,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Projected year business income
rubrics_metrics.description: The business must expect a total gross income of less than $150,000 in the current calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-owned small business — Ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor or the inventor-owned small business must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the application or resulting patent to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply — clearinghouse role and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB Bar Association is the clearinghouse for this program and will review completed applications to determine if the applicant meets the eligibility qualifications and any additional requirements for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the clearinghouse determines that the applicant satisfies all the eligibility requirements, the clearinghouse will attempt to match the applicant with a volunteer attorney. The clearinghouse itself does not provide legal advice or representation. The size and scope of this program is limited, and the clearinghouse may not have a suitable volunteer available for every qualified applicant. Qualifying for the program does not guarantee that the applicant will receive representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How patent practitioners can volunteer
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners interested in volunteering should complete an online volunteer application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered patent practitioners are critical to the success of the PTAB Pro Bono Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working relationship guidance for inventors and volunteer practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: After an inventor and a volunteer practitioner begin working together, it is important that they form a good relationship built on trust, honesty, and openness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO provides documents with helpful tips for inventors and volunteer practitioners to consider employing when working together to strengthen their working relationship (e.g., 'Tips for working with a pro bono client' and 'Tips for working with a pro bono practitioner').
